mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months in at least 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for three consecutive months, combined with falling industrial production (INDPRO), signals deteriorating labor and production conditions, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% for three consecutive months AND INDPRO < previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing risk-free rates and increasing present value of future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 2% in a single month after being above 2% for three prior months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and cost of goods, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change < -0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous year's average, coupled with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals a shift from consumption to savings, which reduces demand for equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year average for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 monthly change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or increase policy rates, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) during triggered episodes in at least 60% of cases.
